Setup (steps 1 to 3 prepare the instrument; do them once).

1. Assign Oilcan 1 to channel 1 and set its range to steps 1–64 (see Channel Length). Leave Rate at /1.

2. Set 90 BPM: open Song tasks, choose Tempo & feel, turn E3 to 90 and press K3.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Snap note masks to scale to Off, then return to Mosaic. MIDI 37 (C#1) is not in C major and would otherwise be snapped to a scale note.


Main hits (steps 4 to 7 build and audition the bar without ghost notes).

Ghost notes (steps 8 to 10 add the quiet hit to bars 3 and 4).

8. Return to Pattern Trig and tap step 44 (step 12 of bar 3) and step 60 (step 12 of bar 4).

9. Open Masks and hold step 44. Select Note and turn E3 to MIDI 38 (D1), then select Vel and set 35, then release step 44. Repeat both edits on step 60: first Note 38, then Vel 35.

10. Press Play. Bars 1 and 2 are unchanged. In bars 3 and 4 you hear a quiet third timbre one step before each MIDI 37 accent. Press Stop.


Undo (step 11 returns to the main-only phrase).

11. Open Masks, hold step 44 or 60 and press K2 to remove the values you set, then remove its trig on Pattern Trig.

At probability 50, each ghost onset may play or be skipped on each pass, so evaluate the range of outcomes over several loops instead of expecting a fixed recording.

**Set a dependable main beat.** Select channel 1 and open Channel tasks → Trig params. Turn E2 to a slot, press K2, turn E3 to Trig Probability, press K3. With no step held, set the channel default to 100. Check: every main hit remains eligible on every pass.

**Try the optional variation.** Set steps 44 and 60 to 50 and play several loops. The musical result to listen for is a quiet pickup that appears on some passes and leaves space on others, while the main hits stay present. Which ghost hit appears can differ each loop; no particular pass or captured result is promised.

Restore the fixed comparison by setting both steps to 100, or remove a lock by holding its step and pressing K2. For a captured 0/100 probability example, see Trig Probability, “Turn chance into explicit rests.”

Build a four-bar loop on three channels: Oilcan 1 plays drums on channel 1, Polyperc 1 plays a bass line on channel 2 and Doubledecker plays chords on channel 3. The drum and bass phrases repeat unchanged in every bar. Only the chord roots change, in bar 4, so you hear the harmony move while the groove stays put. Play "Rhythm, bass and a changing chord" under Listen to hear the finished result first.

Before you start:

1. Set 90 BPM in Song tasks → Tempo & feel (E3, then K3). Keep the default Rate /1 on every channel: one step is a sixteenth note, 16 steps are one bar and 64 steps are four bars.

2. Set the range of channels 1–3 to steps 1–64.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Snap note masks to scale to Off, so that MIDI 37 (C#1) in the drum channel is not snapped to C major.

How notes are entered in these recipes: open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). E2 chooses the value (Trig, Note, Vel, Len, Chd1–Chd4). With no step held, E3 sets the channel default, which every step uses unless it has its own value. Hold K1 and tap a step to add or remove a trig on it. Hold a step and turn E3 to give that step its own value. Hold a step and press K2 to remove its own values. The grid shows sixteen steps at a time: bar 1 is steps 1–16, bar 2 is steps 17–32, bar 3 is steps 33–48 and bar 4 is steps 49–64, so move to the right sixteen-step page before you tap steps in a later bar. In bars after the first, add 16 to each step number of bar 1.

Build the channels in order: Percussion Channel, Bass Channel, Chord Channel. Press Play after each one to hear the loop grow before you add the next channel.

Finish with a contrasting section: open the Song Editor, copy the song slot and mute one channel in the copy (see Song Composition). Numeric MIDI notes are used throughout, because Masks shows MIDI 36, 48 and 60 as C1, C2 and C3 while other controls label octaves differently. Each n.b. player is unique: Polyperc 1 cannot be assigned to another channel once it is assigned to the bass.

Part 1 builds the upper phrase on channel 1, part 2 builds the bass on channel 2, part 3 prepares the second key and part 4 performs the change. In the note page, the column is the step and the row is the degree: y=7 is degree 0 (I), y=6 is degree 1 (II) and y=3 is degree 4 (V).

Part 1: upper phrase

1. Set 90 BPM (Song tasks, Tempo & feel, E3, K3). Leave Rate at /1.

2. Open the Scale editor (4,8). Slot 1 at (1,3) is the applied slot. Check Root C and Scale Major on the Scale screen; if you change either, press K3 to save it.

3. Assign Doubledecker to channel 1. Open Pattern Trig, select pattern 1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13.

4. Open Pattern Note (tap Pattern (5,8) until Note is shown) and set the degrees: tap (1,7), (5,7) and (9,7) for degree 0, and (13,6) for degree 1. Set the channel range to steps 1-16.

5. Open Masks. Leave Note at X. Set Vel to 80 and Len to ½. Hold step 13 and set Vel to 50, then release. The phrase ends with a softer last note. Checkpoint: press Play and listen. In C major the upper phrase is MIDI 60, 60, 60, 62. Press Stop before building the bass channel.

Part 2: bass

6. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 2 and select pattern 2 for the channel. On pattern 2, tap steps 1 and 9 on Pattern Trig, then on Pattern Note tap (1,7) for degree 0 and (9,3) for degree 4. Set the range to steps 1-16 and the channel octave to -1 with (9,8).

7. Open Masks with channel 2 selected, leave Note at X, set Vel to 60 and Len ½. Checkpoint: press Play. The bass adds MIDI 48 on beat 1 and MIDI 55 on beat 3 under the upper phrase. Press Stop before preparing slot 2.

Part 3: prepare the second key

8. While stopped, open the Scale editor. Hold K1 and press slot 2 at (2,3) to select it for editing without applying it. On the Scale screen set Root to D and Scale to Major with E2 and E3, and press K3 to save the slot. Slot 1 stays applied, so playback is still C major.

Part 4: perform the change (choose one)

9a. Stopped: play two bars in C major and stop. Short-press slot 2 at (2,3) to apply D major and play two more bars.

9b. Live: while playing, short-press slot 2 at (2,3) at the end of bar 2.

Result check: in D major the upper phrase becomes MIDI 62, 62, 62, 64 and the bass becomes MIDI 50 and 57: the same rhythm moved up a whole tone. Short-press slot 1 at (1,3) to restore C major.

Some synths smooth incoming CC values. A filter or level change sent at the same moment as a note then arrives late and glides through the start of the note. Lock lead time sends each step's lock values slightly before the step so they have settled when the note sounds. The notes themselves keep their timing.

1. Tap K1 briefly and open the norns PARAMS menu.
2. Open MOSAIC and select **Lock lead time (ms)** in the Parameter locks section.
3. Turn E3 to set the required lead time. The menu displays the selected value.
4. Return to Mosaic to compare playback.

Worked values at 130 BPM, where one clock pulse lasts about 4.8 ms. A lead of 0 sends each lock value with its note. A lead of 25 sends it about 28.8 ms ahead (6 pulses). A lead of 50 sends it about 52.9 ms ahead (11 pulses). Listen for the filter or parameter change landing before the note starts instead of sweeping through its attack.
This global setting accepts 0–50 ms and defaults to **25 ms**. It gives MIDI CC/NRPN
parameter locks time to settle before the note attack, particularly on devices
that smooth incoming controllers. Set it to **0** to send each value at its own
step, which is the original output timing. The value is saved with Mosaic's
project settings.

A step's parameter values leave ahead of the step, in an earlier clock pulse.
Nothing is delayed to achieve this: note-ons, note-offs, live MIDI-thru, outgoing
MIDI Clock, Start, Continue, Stop and song position all keep the timing they have
at a lead of 0, and gate lengths are unchanged. N.b. players are unaffected.

Because a value leaves on a clock pulse, the wait it achieves is the setting
rounded **up** to the next whole pulse, so a value never leaves with less lead
than was asked for. At 130 bpm a pulse is about 4.8 ms, so a 25 ms setting
delivers about 28.8 ms; at 200 bpm it delivers 25 ms exactly. The figure follows
the tempo, and every value of a step leaves on the same pulse, so what you hear
stays consistent between events rather than fixed to the number in the menu.

No step is looked ahead musically: probability, conditions, fills, random notes,
strum, arps and micro-timing still make their decisions at their own times. Only
the parameter values a step will send are resolved early.

Every note sounds with its own step's values. When two notes on the same MIDI
channel are less than twice the lead apart (a fast tempo, a fast channel clock,
or swing and shuffle bringing steps together), a value does not take the whole
lead: it waits until halfway between the previous sounding note and its own step.
The previous note keeps its value through the first half of the gap, and the new
value settles in the second half. A trigless step sounds nothing, so it is not
the note a later value waits behind. A strummed chord's later voices are sounding
notes, so the next step's values wait behind the last of them.

An address that more than one slot writes, whether two slots of one channel or
two channels addressing one device parameter, is not sent early: its values leave
at their own step, in the order the step would send them at a lead of 0.

Two cases give no lead at all. The first step after Play resolves its lock on the
transport's own first pulse, so there is no earlier pulse for its values to leave
in and they leave with the note. A parameter that is mid-slide keeps its slide
until the slide's destination step, so that step's lock arrives with the step
rather than before it. Nothing is delayed to hide either case.

The lead covers the time a receiver takes for a parameter change to take effect,
so every value follows the same rule whether or not its step has a note: trigless
locks, assigned values and slide values leave ahead of the step they belong to and
take effect as that step is heard.

Editing a lock that has already left changes what the next pass sends, and the
edited value is sent again at its own step, so the receiver is corrected rather
than left holding the superseded value. Mosaic restores its output hooks on
cleanup; stop and panic release held voices without leaving queued output behind.

Channel count, clock rate, trig locks, parameter slides and n.b. devices affect Mosaic’s workload. Heavy workload can delay sequencing and make external clock synchronization unreliable.

- Use greater care with high clock rates, trig locks, parameter slides and n.b. devices as channel count increases.
- High clock rates and multipliers increase sequencer workload.
- Use global parameter slides sparingly. Use step parameter slides when global sliding is unnecessary, and limit the total number of slides.
- Disable trigless locks when the additional modulation granularity is not needed.
- Limit the number of n.b. devices.

Other combinations can produce different results. This earlier example does not specify a universal limit for the current version.

Starting point: Use a separate empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and C major, with playback stopped. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1 and Doubledecker to channel 2. Give each channel range 1–16.

**Controls and map.** Press Channel at (3,8), select its number on row 1 and turn E1 to Channel tasks. Use E2 and K3 to open Device, Masks or Trig params. On Device, E2 selects a row, E3 selects the sound and K3 applies it. On Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel or Len and E3 changes the value. Hold a step while turning E3 for a local value; hold K1 and tap a step to add a trig. Steps 1–16 are row 4, 17–32 row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7; the column is its position within that group (step 33 is (1,6), step 61 is (13,7)). Hold the first step and tap the last to set a channel range, then release. For Song slots, press Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are (1,1)–(3,1). Hold the source slot, tap the destination, release, then tap the destination to edit it. On the length fader, (3,7) gives 13 steps and three taps at (8,7) give 16; (4,7) gives 32 and (7,7) gives 64. In Song Tempo and feel (E1 tasks, E2 task, K3), set Tempo to 90 and press K3. Set each channel Rate /1 on its Clock page and apply with K3. In Trig params, E2 selects a slot, K2 opens its assignment list, E3 highlights a parameter, K3 assigns it and K2 returns. Hold a step and turn E3 to set its lock; K2 clears a held-step lock. Stop before copying or editing an independent comparison.

**Prepare the two patterns.** On channel 1, create pattern 1 with trigs 1, 5, 9 and 13; set their degrees to 0, 0, 4 and 0. Set channel 1 octave to -1, velocity to 70 and length to half a step. On channel 2, create pattern 2 with trigs 3, 7, 11 and 15; set their degrees to 4, 2, 4 and 6. Set channel 2 octave to 0, velocity to 60 and length to half a step. Checkpoint: in C major the bass is MIDI 48, 48, 55, 48 and the lead is MIDI 67, 64, 67, 71.

**Slot 1 — intro.** In Song Editor set slot 1 length to 16 steps and mute channel 2 with K1 plus its selector (2,1). Check: slot 1 is one bar of bass with the lead muted.

**Slot 2 — verse.** Copy slot 1 to slot 2, set slot 2 length to 32 steps and toggle channel 2 back on. Check: the two-bar verse has both parts; bass remains 48, 48, 55, 48 and lead remains 67, 64, 67, 71.

**Slot 3 — outro.** Copy slot 2 to slot 3 and set slot 3 length to 16 steps. Set channel 2 octave to +1 and channel 1 Velocity to 40. Check: the one-bar outro keeps the same four bass pitches at lower velocity and raises the lead to MIDI 79, 76, 79, 83.

Play the three slots in order, then Stop and select slot 1. The arrangement is intro (bass only), verse (bass and lead), outro (higher lead and softer bass). This is a separate arrangement example; return to the continuing course project when finished.

Lock random to pent. is On by default. This recipe lets you hear what it does by switching it Off and On with Random Note at 4. Random Note chooses its offsets at random, so listen to several loops: a short run may not include every note.

Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) in C major; no Trig params slot is assigned yet.

1. Assign Random Note. Select channel 1 and turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Trig params and press K3. Press K2 to open the parameter list, turn E3 to Random Note, press K3 to assign it to the first slot and press K2 to return. The slot reads 0 and the pattern still plays C, D, E, F.

2. Set the amount. With the Random Note slot selected (E2), turn E3 four detents right to 4. Each note is now offset by -2, -1, 0, +1 or +2 scale degrees at random. A step that draws offset 0 keeps its own note.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock random to pent. and turn E3 to Off. Close the menu, tap Play and listen to several loops: F and B join the random notes, and one of them will turn up within a few passes. Tap Play to stop.

4. Turn Lock random to pent. On and play several loops again. The random notes now stay on C, D, E, G and A. A step that draws offset 0 keeps its own note, so a plain F in the pattern can still sound. The random stream is not reset between the two runs, so the two runs will not start with the same notes; compare which notes occur, not the order.

Use this option to keep generated, random or merged material consonant: with Lock all to pent. On, every note lands on the five-note version of the scale. The seven-note walk below is a diagnostic rather than a phrase, so you can hear exactly which degrees are replaced. Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) in C major.

1. Build seven degrees. Press Pattern (5,8), select pattern 1 (1,1) and tap trigs on steps 5, 6 and 7 at (5,4), (6,4) and (7,4). Press Pattern (5,8) again for the note page and tap (5,3), (6,2) and (7,1) to put steps 5 to 7 on degrees V, VI and VII: steps 1 to 7 now form a rising diagonal.

2. Set the range. Press Channel (3,8), hold step 1 (1,4), tap step 7 (7,4) and release both. Tap Play (1,8) and listen: 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71. Tap Play to stop.

On Device, E2 selects a row, E3 selects the sound and K3 applies it. On Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel or Len and E3 changes the value. Hold a step while turning E3 for a local value; hold K1 and tap a step to add a trig. Steps 1–16 are row 4, 17–32 row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7; the column is its position within that group (step 33 is (1,6), step 61 is (13,7)). Hold the first step and tap the last to set a channel range, then release. For Song slots, press Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are (1,1)–(3,1). Hold the source slot, tap the destination, release, then tap the destination to edit it. On the length fader, (3,7) gives 13 steps and three taps at (8,7) give 16; (4,7) gives 32 and (7,7) gives 64. In Song Tempo and feel (E1 tasks, E2 task, K3), set Tempo to 90 and press K3. Set each channel Rate /1 on its Clock page and apply with K3. In Trig params, E2 selects a slot, K2 opens its assignment list, E3 highlights a parameter, K3 assigns it and K2 returns. Hold a step and turn E3 to set its lock; K2 clears a held-step lock. Stop before copying or editing an independent comparison.

**Prepare the two patterns.** On channel 1, create pattern 1 with trigs 1, 5, 9 and 13; set their degrees to 0, 0, 4 and 0. Set channel 1 octave to -1, velocity to 70 and length to half a step.
